newsitem.title: UK: Briton asks for Moslem help in freeing hostage.
newsitem.headline: Briton asks for Moslem help in freeing hostage.

text.p: The partner of a Briton held hostage in Kashmir for more than a year urged Moslems on Sunday to help secure his freedom.
Catherine Moseley made her emotional appeal to Moslems gathering at London's Hyde Park Corner to protest at their Islamic fundamentalist rally being called off for security reasons.
She urged Moslems around the world to push for the release of her partner Paul Wells and other westerners kidnapped in July 1995 by militants demanding the release of Kashmiri separatists.
"I believe they are still alive, I have to believe that Paul and the others will be safely returned to their families," she told the park gathering.
Militant Syrian Omar Bakri-Mohammed's al-Muhajiroun group had originally planned to hold its "Rally for Revival" at a 12,000-seat arena in the east of the British capital.
It was called off at the last moment because the organisation was asked to pay thousands of pounds (dollars) for extra security after foreign governments urged Britain to ban the meeting.
Britain issued a stern warning to the organisers that it would not tolerate statements supporting terrorism, but said it had no powers to prevent the meeting.

Al-Muhajiroun has called for a holy war against Middle East governments and its leader urged his listeners not to forget the principles of Islam and the jihad (holy war) and said one day Britain and the whole world would be governed by Islam.
A British gay rights group held a rival rally at Speaker's Corner in protest at al-Muhajiroun's call for the death penalty on homosexuals.
Peter Tatchell of the group OutRage said: "We believe it is very important to visibly challenge Al-Muhajiroun.
"They seem to be putting on a respectable face today, but we know from their past pronouncements that they are violently anti-semitic and homophobic."
